raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Preserve a Uniform KV group's full per-layer specs when building the scheduler cache config, so native offloading sees the same physical pages and canonical-layout eligibility as workers.

## Claims

- Keep heterogeneous page accounting consistent between scheduler and worker for spec-derived and HiSparse indexer sizing.
- Reject canonical storage when a non-portable sibling is hidden by the scheduler's representative MLA spec.
- Reuse the existing `kv_tp_replicas` protocol from #57652; the replicated-layout gate and default options are unchanged.

## Validation

**Draft:** human line-by-line review and accelerator end-to-end/model validation are pending.

| Check | Base | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three new offloading regressions | 3 failed | 3 passed |
| Offloading config + selected scheduler/planning tests | — | 97 passed |
| GPU/NPU end-to-end and model evaluation | Not run | Pending hardware validation |

Reproduced against base `77d2790e788ec323c8bc1fcee72013b363bd9957` with the new tests copied into a detached worktree:

```bash
uv run --offline --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest   tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py   -k 'heterogeneous_pages or canonical_certification_keeps' -q
# Base: 3 failed, 78 deselected.
# Patched: 3 passed, 78 deselected.
```

The baseline reports scheduler/worker byte mismatches for both parameter values and incorrectly certifies the sharded sibling as parallelism agnostic.

Relevant baseline output:

```text
test_heterogeneous_pages_keep_scheduler_worker_offload_sizes[False]
E AssertionError: assert 65536 == 40960
test_heterogeneous_pages_keep_scheduler_worker_offload_sizes[True]
E AssertionError: assert 8192 == 6144
test_canonical_certification_keeps_all_layer_specs
E AssertionError: assert not True
3 failed, 78 deselected
```


```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 uv run --offline --no-project   .venv/bin/python -m pytest   tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py   tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py   tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py   -k 'test_config or generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config or kv_tp_replicas or kv_cache_groups_tp_replicas' -q
# 97 passed.
```

Ruff 0.14.0, Python compilation, YAML parsing, whitespace checks, and the repository test-tethering check passed. Full pre-commit initialization timed out while fetching its GitHub hook environment; it is not reported as passing. The Buildkite KV-offload step now selects the offloading config tests and covers connector-source changes.

No accelerator is available locally. Unit results do not establish serving correctness or model accuracy; human line-by-line review, hardware end-to-end validation, and model evaluation remain pending before this draft is ready for review.

## Details

`generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config()` replaces `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` with its first layer's spec. The offloading translator could then multiply that page by the layer count, or certify canonical MLA storage without inspecting the other layers. Tensor-backed ordinary sizing already uses allocation sizes; the sizing fix concerns the spec-derived fallback and HiSparse path.

Keep the original Uniform in an optional `KVCacheGroupSpec.full_kv_cache_spec` field while retaining the representative used by scheduler block management. Offloading consults the full layout for page accounting and per-layer certification. Projection remains idempotent and does not mutate worker configs.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-11-03 covered open PRs for offloading/scheduler, Uniform specs, full_kv_cache_spec, and representative/per-layer accounting. #56953 changes multi-group slot accounting and leaves the single-group case unchanged; #55810 changes GLM hybrid grouping/padding. Neither preserves the scheduler's folded per-layer layout. Closed #56772/#56799 addresses canonical secondary row portability. This change complements the already merged #57652.

Related Ascend metadata fix: [vllm-ascend#20766](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20766). That fix uses the already-existing replication protocol and does not depend on this scheduler-projection change.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for analysis, implementation, tests, and this description.

@@ -22,6 +22,20 @@ flowchart LR
     CPU <--> SN["..."]
 ```
 
+## Replicated MLA cache
+
+On a single node using the multiprocessing executor, the native CPU primary
+tier can store one copy of KV that is fully replicated across tensor-parallel
+ranks. This also applies to MLA models with a separate replicated sparse
+attention indexer. The CPU capacity then holds one complete block instead
+of one copy per rank, including every indexer page and its quantization scales.
+
+This requires TP > 1, PP = PCP = DCP = 1, and every layer's cache to be
+declared fully replicated by the model backend. Hybrid models with sharded
+or unknown cache state keep separate copies. The optimization requires a
+shared host region; platform implementations using process-local host
+allocations keep their per-worker layout.
+
 ## Per-request load control
 
 Individual requests can cap how many tokens are loaded from offloaded storage
